sentences.text: Cathayornis yandica was a small bird featuring an elongated, toothy beak and feet specifically adapted for perching.
Like other Enantiornithes, a group of early birds, this animal possessed large claws on its first two wing fingers used for support.
It is distinguished from similar birds like Sinornis by its larger size and a shorter, straighter first finger with a longer claw.
Only one definitive fossil specimen, catalogued as IVPP V9769, is currently known for Cathayornis yandica.
Cathayornis yandica serves as the type species, meaning it is the specific species upon which the entire genus Cathayornis is based.
The genus Cathayornis was originally described by Zhou, Jin, and Zhang in 1992.
This discovery made Cathayornis yandica one of the first Enantiornithes species identified in China.
However, several species previously assigned to Cathayornis have since been reclassified or deemed invalid.
In 2002, Paul Sereno and colleagues classified Cathayornis as a junior synonym of Sinornis, a taxonomic decision that remains part of the scientific discussion.
Cathayornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Specific dating places the animal between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Its fossils come from the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.

Researchers questioned the validity of Cathayornis aberransis, a species previously assigned to the genus, after finding its distinguishing features, such as a skull crest, were inaccurately described.
